window.note: Why a second model had to be trained. Each condition needs an answer sentence and a passage of the same length in the window at once. The answer sentences here run to about 120 characters, so the pair needs roughly 240 -- more than Session 1's Machine B has. At a context of 128 the passage would be cut away entirely and the experiment would measure truncation instead of reading. At 256 both fit. Retrieved chunks are longer still, which is a separate point the chunking table makes: a reader small enough to train in a lab cannot hold a whole retrieved paragraph either.
